html:
The Peninsular War, from 1807 to 1814, was fought in Spain and Portugal between France and the allied forces of Spain, Portugal and Britain. Spaniards call it the War of Independence.

Napoleon sent troops into Spain on the way to invade Portugal, then forced the Spanish king to abdicate and made his brother Joseph king in 1808. On 2 May 1808 the people of Madrid rose, and the French shot many in reprisal, a scene painted by Goya. Spanish irregulars waged a guerrilla war, a word first used then. A British army under Wellington, based behind the Lines of Torres Vedras, drove the French out by 1814.

The war cost hundreds of thousands of lives. In Cádiz a free parliament wrote the liberal constitution of 1812. With Spain in chaos, its American colonies began to break away. The war was part of the Napoleonic Wars. See Spain.
sum: The Peninsular War, from 1807 to 1814, was fought in Spain and Portugal between France and the allied forces of Spain, Portugal and Britain. Spaniards call it the War of Independence.
